messages.subject: Question about accessing local files.
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

My name is Chungha Sung who is the one of members developing an R libarary called RIGHT for interactive visualization using JavaScript and HTML5 canvas. I think you may remember that JungHoon Lee asked a question about 'shiny.onInputchange'. Thanks to your suggestion, Our team developed a simple package and uploaded it on CRAN. Also, we are trying to refine it further to make a complete package, and we will promote it.

While I am refining it, I am stuck on a problem about browser security. Our package should access local files for analysising data on JavaScript part. However, before changing local files security policy of browsers(e.g. add flag "--allow-file-access-from-files" on chrome. You can understand it by seeing this <https://code.google.com/p/r-interactive-graphics-via-html/wiki/FAQs>), an error occurs with "XMLHttpRequest cannot load file.." in JavaScript console.
I am using this code for access to local file.

var filePath = fileName;
xmlhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();
xmlhttp.open("GET", filePath, false);
xmlhttp.send(null);

The shiny packge may have same problems, I guess. Could you give me some suggestions or advice to solve this problem? Do you have any method to avoid it?
If you have it, do you mind letting us know where the file access part is in your code?
If you know something, please help us to solve it. It will be very helpful.

Thank you very much in advance!

Sincerely,
Chungha Sung

messages.subject: Re: Progress Bar Not Showing
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have the same problem : I don't see the progress bar.

I add "progressInit()" function inside my ui.R.

I developed in Shiny local Server on ubuntu 12.04 and Chrome.

Server.R
library(shiny)
library(shinyIncubator)

shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {
    output$test <- renderPlot({

    withProgress(session, min=1, max=15, {
 setProgress(message = 'Calculation in progress', detail = 'This may take a while...')
 for (i in 1:15) {
   print(i)
   setProgress(value = i)
   Sys.sleep(0.5)
 }
})

    plot(1,1)
    })
})

ui.R

library(shinyIncubator)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

.......

  # Show the caption and plot of the requested variable against mpg
  mainPanel(

    tabsetPanel(
 tabPanel("test1",plotOutput("test")),
           progressInit(),
           tabPanel("test2",plotOutput("test")),
)
  )
))

I installed shinyIncubator package with this command line :

sudo su - -c "R -e \"devtools::install_github('shiny-incubator', 'rstudio')\""

messages.subject: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hello Shiny enthusiasts,

I was building a new shiny app, when I realised that I make use a lot of GoogleVis Tables and that this might not be the best way.
Especially if you have a lot of reactivity, those tables sometimes unsystematically do not appear.

So I am looking for a more reliable alternative with equal visual niceness, usability (easy to implement) and functionality.

What kind of table solution do you prefer in what situation?

Let the knowledge expand
(all your brains are belong to us)

1) This line: qry <- "select SECURITYKEY from usersessiontracking where User_Name = '" + username + "'" should be replaced with this: qry <- "select SECURITYKEY from usersessiontracking where User_Name = '" + dbEscapeStrings(con, username) + "'" Otherwise, it would be easy for an attacker to type in their name as foo';DROP DATABASE srinergi_sales;-- and you would lose your whole database. This is called SQL injection and you must give careful thought to avoiding it whenever you put database-accessing apps in users' hands. 2) In the future I highly recommend you NOT posting a real username/password to a public forum or mailing list!! 3) You are calling dbDisconnect before you actually fetch your data. I'd recommend taking out that dbDisconnect call, and instead, immediately after the line with dbConnect, add the line: on.exit(dbDisconnect(con)) This way, it will properly close the connection even if an exception occurs. messages.subject: Re: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
I also recently switched my app from using Gvis tables to data tables in rCharts.  The only downside to the rCharts version is it can take a while to load if it has more than a few thousand rows (mine had 8 columns and ~15k rows, ended up just cutting it down to the top 1000 rows to speed things up).  However, after the initial load time, the switching between pages and doing searches is instantaneous.

messages.body_plain:
We are adding bindings for datatables <http://www.datatables.net> to Shiny itself in the next release (0.8.0?). The bindings know how to do server-based pagination, so you should be able to get good performance even for very large tables.

However, after the initial load time, the switching between pages and doing searches is instantaneous.

messages.subject: Well Panel Field Width CSS
messages.body_plain:
I'm having trouble tracking down the source for a visual issue in my shiny app. As a disclaimer...I know next to nothing about CSS and am still learning. Based on other examples...I have attempted to create a reactive wellPanel containing two side-by-side lists of objects that a user selects to filter the output.

While being rendered on my native laptop display (1366 x 768)...the selectInput() dropdown lists in the wellPanel behave as I intend (the two selectInput lists are located side-by-side and are discrete/do not overlap). I have noted a visual display "bug" where when I display the shiny app on a projector via VGA input from a laptop...the screen resolution changes and sidebarPanel() changes size while the selectInput() fields in the wellPanel remain their original/specified size/width and end up overlapping resulting in obscured selectInput() fields (see example images below).

My question is...how do I make the size of the selectInput() fields dynamic so they scale proportionally regardless of the display (or is this even possible)?

Example snippets of code that influence the appearance of the wellPanel()

server.R
#defines the two lists used in the wellPanel()
output$date_list <- renderUI({
> selectInput("date_list","Syn Date:",choices=filtered_all()$syndate)
})

output$plate_select <- renderUI({
> selectInput("plate_select","Syn Plate:",choices=plate_list())
 })

ui.R
widget_style <- "display: inline-block;
                  vertical-align: text-top;
                  padding: 7px;
                  border: solid;
                  border-width: 1px;
                  border-radius: 4px;
                  border-color: #CCC;"

conditionalPanel(
                  condition = "input.conditioned_panels == 2",
                  wellPanel(
                        h5("Single Plate Spatial Analysis:"),
                        div(class="row-fluid",
                            div(style = widget_style, uiOutput("date_list")),
                            div(style=widget_style, uiOutput("plate_select"))),
                        tags$style(type="text/css", '#date_list {width: 125px}'),
                        tags$style(type="text/css", '#plate_select {width: 150px}'),
                        helpText("Select synthesis date & plate barcode.")
                   ))

What I have tried so far:

By trial and error...I have determined that I can change the "px" argument in the  '#date_list {width: 125px}' or  '#plate_select {width: 150px}' fields to a lower specified value but it does not solve the root problem of makig the field dynamic.
If I remove the two tag$style arguments altogether...the two selectInput() fields stack on top of each other which is also undesired behavior.
Any advice/help is greatly appreciated!

library(rCharts)

> I have shiny 0.7.0 running on an Ubuntu 12.04.2 LTS machine. When I launch an app using Chrome browser, three processes get created. However, when I close the browser window, the three processes persist. The processes don't end until I manually kill them using sudo killall R. Because of this issue a few apps that use Sys.Date() to popualte dateInput() are not refreshing the date. For example, if I clear all processes using the killall command and launch the app today, it will show today's date (9/30/2013) correctly. Now if I close the browser and launch it again tomorrow, it will show 9/30/2013 instead of tomorrow's date (10/1). If I then kill the processes, it will show tomorrow's date correctly.

> The discussion in the "Persistent R session" thread was about this problem occurring in Ubuntu 13.04. Does anyone know why this might be happening in 12.04.2 LTS?

messages.subject: Re: Well Panel Field Width CSS
messages.body_plain:
It is hard to help you without having access to a page. Have you tried using "%" (percent of a parent frame width) instead of "px"? It is also may be due to font size, you can use "em" if you want your interface to scale with the font. Or you could try to set a fixed font size. Check out CSS unit reference <http://www.w3schools.com/cssref/css_units.asp>

messages.subject: Re: Progress Bar Not Showing
messages.body_plain:
Determining the max value is completely up to the user. However if you can't tell, you can just not specify anything and just call setProgress(message="..."), in which case just the message will update and not the bar.

>
> How can i indicate at user while data are not ready, a progressBar is shown during all calculation time ?
>
> Server.R
>
> output$table <- renderTable({
>       withProgress(session, min=1, max=20, {
>  setProgress(message = 'Calculation in progress', detail = 'This may take a while...')

>    print(i)
>    setProgress(value = i)
>    Sys.sleep(0.5)
>  }
> })

messages.subject_clean: Recent Chrome update is causing immediate drop of local host:8100 connection.
messages.body_plain:
I have had a large Shiny based GUI working for several months.  It connected to Chrome, Firefox, and Safari using localhost:8100 as the URL.

Within the last day or two, Chrome did an update and now when I try to use it to connect to the Shiny app, it momentarily connects, showing the expected widgets, then it goes gray.  This behavior repeats when a refresh is done.

For what it's worth, I have this behavior on IE10, but just chalked it up to a Microsoft idiosyncrasy.  Now I think I may have done IE10 a disservice.

if (!require(maps))

messages.subject: Re: Progress Bar Not Showing
messages.body_plain:
You could set the min/max value from 0 to 1, and then send fractional units.

withProgress(session, min=0, max=1, {
  setProgress(message = "Loading user data...")
  workToDo = loadUserData()
  # Let's say we normally expect the user data loading to take 20% of the total time
  setProgress(value = 0.2, message = "Calculating...")
  jobLength = length(workToDo)
  for (i in 1:jobLength) {
    # Do work
    setProgress(0.2 + (i / jobLength))
  }
})

messages.subject: Reactivity / Chain Reaction Question
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,

This is a Reactivity / Chain Reaction Question...
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Working on a Shiny app which uses many reactive functions.
Below I have a screenshot that shows three reactive functions.

The first two reactive functions (which set 'k' and 'timing') are both dependent on input$timingType.
The third reactive function (which sets GSD) is dependent on the first two ('k' and 'timing').

I understand that when input$timingType changes, it causes the reactive functions 'k' and 'timing' to fire.
My question is...Does that mean that GSD function will fire twice...the first time for the 'k' value change and the second time for the 'timing' value?

It is hopeful (for performance issues) that the GSD function only gets called once after both 'k' and 'timing' are set.
Please write with your thoughts/tricks/best practices.

 <https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-6ieeOeGswSU/UlC-Sg2KXKI/AAAAAAAAAaY/PoGIIlOH3Tw/s1600/Screen+Shot+2013-10-05+at+9.33.48+PM.png>
John

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity / Chain Reaction Question
messages.body_plain:
TL;DR: It won't in most cases.

I am going to explain this from my understanding. Pro-Shiny-Users please correct me if I am wrong.

As far as reactives go, input changes don't cause them to recalculate, in reactive/Shiny lingo they do not react to flush events (see http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#execution-scheduling)
I will explain what this means, or you can read the tutorial to get the official version.

In this specific instance I believe there would be some outputs (or an observe()) that depend on GSD(). For simplicity suppose there is only one output$something that depends on GSD.

In Shiny A will invalidate B if A was called in the previous run of the code B (you need not understand this in this particular instance but it may help you debug more complex cases later on)

So when your input$timingType changes, it invalidates both k() and timing(), both of these in turn invalidate GSD(). Finally GSD() will invalidate output$something..

One thing to highlight is that invalidation does not cause recalculation, so at this stage no re-calculation has occurred.

Now suppose all things that can be invalidated by the changes to input$timingType has occurred, now a flush event occurs. Once this occurs output$something will re-calculate as it is an endpoint. Since it depends on GSD so somewhere in its code it will call GSD() and this is when GSD() will recalcualte. Now GSD() depends on t() and timing() so inside GSD() both t() and timing() gets called. Now once t() and timing() were both called and their values updated, GDS() will use their values to update itself and now output$something can finish its computation based on GDS().

To summarise when output$something runs, it calls on GSS() which calls on k() and timing(). So each of k(), timing() and GSD() was run only once.

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity / Chain Reaction Question
messages.body_plain:
The above explanation I find a bit convoluted.

When input$timingType changes, it doesn't "fire" timing() and k() in that it causes them rerun, it only invalidates them, the invalidation of timing() and k() will also invalidate GSD(), and GSD() will invalidate output$something. Once everything has been invalidated, a flush event happens. The flush event will attempt to recalculate output$something, which will call GSD() which calls k() and timing().

Things just happen in "reverse" compared to traditional event driven programming, where A fires B fires C. In Shiny/reactive programming it's like A invalidates B invalidates C, flush, fire C, C fires B, B fires A.

> Now suppose all things that can be invalidated by the changes to input$timingType has occurred, now a flush event occurs. Once this occurs output$something will re-calculate as it is an endpoint. Since it depends on GSD so somewhere in its code it will call GSD() and this is when GSD() will recalcualte. Now GSD() depends on t() and timing() so inside GSD() both t() and timing() gets called. Now once t() and timing() were both called and their values updated, GDS() will use their values to update itself and now output$something can finish its computation based on GDS().
>

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity / Chain Reaction Question
messages.body_plain:
I've found the reactive log visualizer to be very helpful for questions like this.
?showReactLog , the tutorial, and a very simple example, run from a fresh R session demonstrates what ZJ explains very clearly (second post ;-)).
Something like:

==> reactive/server.R <==
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  A <- reactive({
    input$n ^ 2
  })

  B <- reactive({
    -input$n
  })

  output$Value <- renderText({
    A() + B()
  })
})

==> reactive/ui.R <==

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Reactive"),

  sidebarPanel(
    numericInput("n", "N:", 10)
  ),

  mainPanel(
    textOutput("Value")
  )
))

Then in a fresh R session,
> require(shiny)
Loading required package: shiny
> options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE)
> runApp("reactive/", port=8101L)

and after you change the input value, type ctrl-F3 and step through the reactive events.

HTH,
David Reiner

messages.subject: Re: Shiny doesn't bind to elements that are 'hidden' when first initializing
messages.subject_clean: Shiny doesn't bind to elements that are 'hidden' when first initializing
messages.body_plain:
Well, it all depends on the initial status:

- if an element is hidden initially, shiny will _always_ ignore it,
even if you .show() it later
- if an element is shown initially, shiny will always use it, even if
you .hide() it later

What I said was, it is not enough to call .show()/.hide() -- you have
to trigger the internal events "shown"/"hidden" of shiny, so that
shiny can refresh its memory about the visibility of that element.

outputOptions(output, 'x', suspendWhenHidden=FALSE) can solve the
problem, but it depends on what you really want: do you want the
hidden elements to react or not? If you do want them to react, then
use suspendWhenHidden=FALSE; if you want to forget about hidden
elements, you need to trigger the shown/hidden events after you
.show()/.hide().

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <yi...@rstudio.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to 'mimic' a table using a multiple select (selectInput(...,multiple=TRUE)) by inserting spaces and vertical bars so that the text in each row lines up. However, I run into the issue that when displayed, the options lose their spacing.

For example, if i have under selectInput('multiSelect','   A|   B',vec.out) with

vec.out = c(1,2,3)
names(vec.out)= c('   1|   2','  11|  22',' 111| 222')

and spaces such that the string is of length 4 to the left and to the right of the bar. The idea is that the multiple select will render such that it resembles a data frame with right justified columns df$A=c(1,11,111) and df$B=c(2,22,222). Unfortunately, the extra blank spaces for the first few rows are shortened to just 1 when the selectInput is rendered.

I've tried doing a gsub to replace all the spaces with   but then all the text is just rendered verbatim, i.e.

   A|   B
   1|   2
  11|  22
 111| 222

How should I go about this?
Thanks,
Ray

messages.subject: Re: Spacing in multiple-select options
messages.body_plain:
So I looked into the underlying code and it seems that the main issue is that somewhere in the selectInput function it escapes '&'s by replacing them with '&amp' string. It is necessary to 'unescape' by having as the last line of selectInput a gsub wrapper which re-replaces '&amps' with '&', i.e. instead of

tagList(controlLabel(inputId, label),selectTag)

replace it with

gsub('&','&',tagList(shiny:::controlLabel(inputId, label), selectTag)).

TL;DR: To preserve spacing, replace all spaces with the nonbreakable space character '&nbsp', then in selectInput replace the final line of code with a gsub operation.

messages.subject: Re: Spacing in multiple-select options
messages.body_plain:
gsub('&','&') does not look good, even though it may work in this
particular case, since it may unescape characters that should have
been escaped, e.g. selectInput('foo', label='Foo&', choices=1:3)

Perhaps selectInput() should provide an additional argument "names"
which is names(choices) by default, and users can also provide
HTML("custom html names") so that the names will not be escaped -- the
preferred approach to preventing character strings from being escaped
is HTML(), but that does not apply to selectInput() at the moment. I
think you can file a feature request to
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Proxy question
messages.body_plain:
I'm configuring an Apache2 reverse proxy in front of a shiny server. I've followed the rstudio proxy example as a starting point.

The rstudio is working fine.  The shiny application will load the non-interactive parts but for the 01_hello example, the histogram will not update. This happens for all the examples.

The shiny server config is all default settings on port 3838.

This is running on a Ubuntu 12 LTS server.

The /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/default for the HTTP settings include a redirect as follows that appears to work. I'm forcing all activity to the SSL side.

        RewriteEngine On
        RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off
        RewriteRule (.*) https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [R]

The /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/default-ssl for HTTPS has the following added:

        <Proxy *>
                Order deny,allow
                Allow from all
        </Proxy>

        RedirectMatch permanent ^/rstudio$ /rstudio/
        <Location /rstudio/>
                ProxyPass        http://localhost:8787/
                ProxyPassReverse http://localhost:8787/
        </Location>

        RedirectMatch permanent ^/shiny$ /shiny/
        <Location /shiny/>
                ProxyPass        http://localhost:3838/
                ProxyPassReverse http://localhost:3838/
        </Location>

PreserveHost breaks RStudio if enabled.

I can confirm the shiny applications work if I hit them directly on localhost on port 3838. They fail in the above redirected proxied state as stated above.

If someone sees something I've missed or any pointers at thing I should look at, I'd appreciate the help.

Thanks.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny doesn't bind to elements that are 'hidden' when first initializing
messages.body_plain:
ok, that makes total sense. Thanks for the information, Yihui!

El martes, 8 de octubre de 2013 18:04:18 UTC+2, Yihui Xie escribió:
> Well, it all depends on the initial status:
>
> - if an element is hidden initially, shiny will _always_ ignore it,
> even if you .show() it later
> - if an element is shown initially, shiny will always use it, even if
> you .hide() it later
>
> What I said was, it is not enough to call .show()/.hide() -- you have
> to trigger the internal events "shown"/"hidden" of shiny, so that
> shiny can refresh its memory about the visibility of that element.
>
> outputOptions(output, 'x', suspendWhenHidden=FALSE) can solve the
> problem, but it depends on what you really want: do you want the
> hidden elements to react or not? If you do want them to react, then
> use suspendWhenHidden=FALSE; if you want to forget about hidden
> elements, you need to trigger the shown/hidden events after you
> .show()/.hide().
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
> --
> Yihui Xie <yi...@rstudio.com>
> Web: http://yihui.name
>
>
> On Tue, Oct 8, 2013 at 1:33 AM, Guillem Vicens <guille...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I am the one that asked in Stackoverflow about this issue. I might be
> > misunderstanding you but you seem to imply this issue should happen every
> > time you use .hide() or .show(). That is not exactly what is happening.
> >
> > If I do not call .hide() in the OnShow event, afterwards I can call both
> > .show() and .hide() as much as I want. Shiny will continue to react to
> > inputs.
> > Only if I do call .hide() in the OnShow event Shiny stops to react to the
> > hidden input, regardless of whether I use .show() or not.
> >

messages.subject: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
messages.subject_clean: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
messages.body_plain:
If we have...

foo <- reactiveValues(alist=list(a=1,b=2),blist=list(x=3,y=4));

You would expect that isolate(foo$alist <- as.list(1:3)) would prevent the invalidation of things that depend on foo$alist, analogously to how reading a variable wrapped in isolate prevents a dependency from being formed. Unfortunately, it does not.

My questions are:

* Is the effect of isolate(foo$alist <- as.list(1:3)) different in any way from the effect of foo$alist <- as.list(1:3) ?

* If there is a function which I want to update foo$alist silently (i.e. without triggering a cascade of invalidation) and there is another function where I do want the normal invalidation behavior on the same variable, is there a way to accomplish that without having to hunt down every observer that depends on foo$alist, and manually suspending it from within the first (silent) function?

messages.subject: Re: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object
messages.subject_clean: Deletion of list values within a reactiveValue object
messages.body_plain:
On Friday, October 4, 2013 5:48:07 AM UTC-5, Willi Fiebranz wrote:
>
> And
>
> list[["2"]] <- NULL
>
> of course deletes the content of the list section but not the section itself.

I do that in some places, and so far it doesn't cause a problem because once you do that, list["2"]] will return NULL until you assign something else to that slot. So will list[["2"]]$foo$xyz. Therefore, if my observer sees a NULL it assumes the value was not initialized and proceeds accordingly. If there is a practical difference between an uninitialized value and a NULL value, you could just use some other placeholder for an uninitialized value such as "".

PS: You'll live a much happier life if you avoid using names that are numerals such as "2" and names that are also the names of base R functions such as "list". It's syntactically valid, but guaranteed to confuse the hell out of you sooner or later.

Example: an observer has a dependency on reactiveList value foo$bar. Under some conditions it writes to foo$bar (e.g. corrects a commonly occurring input error). There is no need for this observer to invalidate itself, though, because we already know the value of foo$bar and presumably acted on it. We want for it to "sit this round out" and wait for something else to update foo$bar and only then invalidate.

messages.subject: Re: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
messages.subject_clean: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
messages.body_plain:
Yes, that's absolutely expected, though unfortunately not that intuitive, I'll admit! Assigning to subelements of values in reactiveValues will necessarily involve both a read and a write. For that reason I tend to write

relog$log[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one');

as

log <- relog$log

log[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one')

relog$log <- log

instead. And indeed this kind of very imperative code needs to be wrapped in isolate!

I'll think about the "sit this round out" problem you mentioned.

On Thu, Oct 10, 2013 at 8:22 PM, Alex Bokov <alex....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Aha!
>
> I found a practical (albeit somewhat edge-casey) consequence of putting an assignment inside isolate() as currently implemented by shiny. The following adds a dynamically named log entry to a reactiveValues object (relog <- reactiveValues(log=list())):
>
> isolate(relog$log[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one'));
>
> ...and somewhere else in the code you can print out the results in a table:
>
> output$log <- renderTable(do.call(rbind,relog$log);
>
> But the following causes whatever called it to go into an endless loop and bring the server to its knees:
>
> relog$log[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one');
>
> I think that the dynamic naming within a reactive object causes this statement to be interpreted as both a read and a write, creating a dependency loop. The fact that isolate() fixes it is how I must have gotten the mistaken idea that isolate does something similar for assign statements in general.
>
> Interestingly, the following does not need isolate() to protect it from loops:
>
> relog2 <- reactiveValues();
> relog2[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one');
> ...
> output$log <- renderTable(do.call(rbind,reactiveValuesToList(relog2)));
>
>
> On Thursday, October 10, 2013 6:32:23 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > No, there absolutely is not and it's hard for me to think of how you could reason about the system at all if we allowed such a thing. What is it you're trying to do?
>

messages.subject_clean: authentication by passing output through php
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joseph,

The value of the Location header is just a URL. So you should be able to just pass back the relative or absolute URL for your Shiny app.

(That said, I don't know enough about your setup to endorse the workflow you've proposed. There will only be a couple of approaches to authentication that we officially bless, and only on the Pro edition of Shiny Server.)

There have certainly been folks who have made this work, though I don't think it's easy. messages.subject: A few questions about reactivity (part 3: can a reactiveValues be destroyed, and what's it made of)
messages.subject_clean: A few questions about reactivity (part 3: can a reactiveValues be destroyed, and what's it made of)
messages.body_plain:
Motivation:

Let's say you've been storing the results of an analysis in a reactiveValues object (named revals). Now the user uploads a new data file, and you want to start from a clean slate. However, from the testing I've done it looks like the following...

observe(if(input$fileupload){ revals <- reactiveValues(); ... })

...only creates a reactiveValues() object within the scope of that expression and it is not accessible from any other reactive context. If I save the shinyServer environment and overwrite revals there...

myenv <- environment();
observe(if(input$fileupload){ myenv$revals <- reactiveValues(); ... })

...that does overwrite the "real" revals but observers with a dependency on revals no longer have access to it from that point on and stop invalidating.

So, what is the proper way to reinitialize a reactiveValues object?

I know that I can iterate over the names of revals and individually NULL them, but that's not a clean solution: there will be named NULL objects left inside of revals, I can't predict what invalidations will get triggered and in what order between the first and the last item to be NULL-ed, and for all I know there might be some other data lingering that exists outside the named objects.

Which brings me to my other question: where does a reactiveValues object reside, and what base R class does it inherit from? Environment? List? Function? Is there perhaps some recommended further documentation to read next after having read the "Understanding Reactivity" section of the Shiny tutorial?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Ace Editor in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
I'm working on a package that may be of interest to this community: shinyAce <https://github.com/trestletech/shinyAce>.

The goal of the package is to enable Shiny applications to take advantage of the Ace editor (the same editor used in the RStudio IDE). For the uninitiated, Ace offers a variety of themes and "modes" (languages). You can sample these modes and themes in this Shiny example <http://bit.ly/160IgdO>. shinyAce supports all of the modes and themes that Ace provides.

Eventually, I hope to setup examples (and integrations) to do Markdown and R code evaluation in this package. (If you can't wait, you can always checkout the example <https://github.com/yihui/knitr/tree/master/inst/shiny> Yihui Xie put together or the hosted OpenCPU application <https://public.opencpu.org/ocpu/library/markdownapp/www/>. Such functionality will eventually be facilitated within this package.)

messages.subject: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?
messages.subject_clean: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I've built a function that at a certain point executes runApp(). Now, I want to be able to pass a couple of input parameters to the function, and want these to be passed on to the shiny app. So running the following command:

myfun(a=1,b=2)

...would result in the following statement being run within the function:

[...]
runApp("myapp")
[...]

And from within the shiny app, i.e. in server.R, I would then want to access the values a and b.

Is there any way to do this? Can I somehow pass the parameters a and b as a list of input parameters to runApp()? Or is the recommended practice to try to access the namespace of myfun()?

I haven't managed to find any answer to this by searching the forum, but if this question's already been answered I'd be grateful if anyone could point me in the right direction :)

Thanks in advance,
Love Hansson

messages.subject: Re: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?
messages.subject_clean: Is there any way to pass input parameters to a shiny app on startup?
messages.body_plain:
If you're embedding runApp() in a larger workflow, you may find this example helpful: https://gist.github.com/trestletech/5948876#file-server-r-L7 . It demonstrates the pattern of assigning a variable outside of a Shiny app then referencing that variable within Shiny.

The "parent" markdown file ("ReconstructGRN.Rmd") is the one that would be executed by the user. It calls "runApp" to run the Shiny application included in the gist. You can see that the Shiny App checks for the existence of the variable "gn" (on the highlighted line in server.R). This variable wasn't ever defined in the Shiny app -- only the parent markdown file.

Jeff

messages.subject: Neat output in the mainPanel
messages.body_plain:
I want an output like this:

Welch t-test
 t =  0.296
 df =  42.986
 p-value =  0.769

But if I write,
return(c("", method, "\n", "t = ", tstat, "\n", "df = ", df, "\n",  "p-value = ", P, "\n"))
I get the result in one line.
Welch t-test  t = 0.296 df = 42.986 p-value = 0.769

If I use the list function, I get an error.
return(list(method, paste("t =",tstat), paste("df =", df), paste("p.value =", P)))

If I use the cat function, I get the fine output in my R console!
cat("", method, "\n", "t = ", tstat, "\n", "df = ", df, "\n",  "p-value = ", P, "\n")

Please someone tell me how I can show the output in the mainPanel.
Since I've been working on this issue for a couple of days, any information would be appreciated.

My ui.R is:
# ----------
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 headerPanel("Title"),
 sidebarPanel(
    numericInput("nx", " Number of the 1st group:", 21),
    numericInput("mx", " Mean of the 1st group:", 61.33333),
    numericInput("sdx", " SD of the 1st group:", 16.43573),
    numericInput("ny", " Number of the 2nd group:", 24),
    numericInput("my", " Mean of the 2nd group:", 59.79167),
    numericInput("sdy", " SD of the 2nd group:", 18.50729),
    checkboxInput("var.equal", "equal variance", FALSE)
),
  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("values"),
    uiOutput("result"))
)
)
# ----------

My server.R file is:
# ----------
library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
sliderValues <- reactive ({

data.frame(
        n = c(input$nx, input$ny),
        Mean = c(input$mx, input$my),
        SD = c(input$sdx, input$sdy),
        stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
 })

my.t <- function(  nx,
                        mx,
                        sdx,
                        ny,
                        my,
                        sdy,
                        var.equal = FALSE,
                        )
{

    if (input$var.equal==T) {
        method <- " Normal t-test"
        df <- input$nx+input$ny-2
        v <- ((input$nx-1)*input$sdx^2+(input$ny-1)*input$sdy^2)/df
        tstat <- round(abs(input$mx-input$my)/sqrt(v*(1/input$nx+1/input$ny)),3)
    }
    else {
        method <- "Welch t-test"
        tstat <- round(abs(input$mx-input$my)/sqrt(input$sdx^2/input$nx+input$sdy^2/input$ny),3)
        df <- round((input$sdx^2/input$nx+input$sdy^2/input$ny)^2/((input$sdx^2/input$nx)^2/(input$nx-1)+(input$sdy^2/input$ny)^2/(input$ny-1)), 3)
    }
    P <- round(2*pt(tstat, df, lower.tail=FALSE),3)

    return(c("", method, "\n", "t = ", tstat, "\n", "df = ", df, "\n",  "p-value = ", P, "\n"))
}

output$values <- renderTable({
    sliderValues()
})

output$result <- renderText(
{my.t(input$nx, input$mx, input$sdx, input$ny, input$myx, input$sdy, input$var.equal)}
)
})
# ----------

messages.subject: Re: Generate PDF report with Shiny-server
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

It's probably created using knitr, here's an example of this :

ui.R :
downloadButton("downloadPDF", "Download the PDF report")

server.R :

output$downloadPDF <- downloadHandler(filename = "your_report.pdf",
                        content = function(file){
                            # generate PDF
                            knit2pdf("report.Rnw")

                            # copy pdf to 'file'
                            file.copy("your_report.pdf", file)

                            # delete generated files
                            file.remove("your_report.pdf", "your_report.tex",
                                        "your_report.aux", "your_report.log")

                            # delete folder with plots
                            unlink("figure", recursive = TRUE)
                        },
                        contentType = "application/pdf"
        )

report.Rnw :

\begin{document}
\title{Custom report}
\maketitle
<<Example chunk, cache=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, prompt=FALSE, out.width='\\linewidth', out.height='\\textheight', fig.width=7, fig.height=4.95>>=
    plot(cars)
@
\end{document}

messages.subject: Re: Table with selectable rows
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kirill (and Joe),

I was very happy to discover this reactive table.

Due to my being an absolute shiny novice, however, I have been stalled for a few hours trying to add a feature.  Perhaps one of you can point me in the right direction?

What I wish to do is

   1) detect the cell that has been clicked (this works fine, of course)
   2) extract the original data from the underlying data.frame (also works)
   3) do some operations on that data (in my case, parse out a pubmed ID, and retrieve the related journal article abstract)
   4) display the text of the abstract in a textarea

In my experiments it would be completely adequate to skip step 3, and just display the data.frame[row,col] value in the  textarea.

I can modify the contents of the target textarea, using some simple jquery added (inelegantly) to responsiveTable.js.
But back in R -- where I need to be, to have access to the data.frame, and to familiar code which can fetch the journal abstract, I do not know how to change the contents of the target textarea.  Perhaps some inline javascript could help do that?  Or is that too much a hack, and I need to define a reactive element that connects the responsiveTable event and the textarea?  If so, are their any examples of that you can suggest?

I suspect that if I had more completely absorbed the reactive programming idiom I would be able to figure out the answer.

Any guidance you can provided will be deeply appreciated!

messages.subject: Re: Shinyapps + rga
messages.body_plain:
Hi Badri,

I'm not familiar with rga, but one well-documented alternative is to use Shiny Server to embed a Google Analytics ID into each app. (see the "google analytics id" section here: http://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config.html#google_analytics_id).

The alternative would be to embed the necessary Javascript in your Shiny application directly. This isn't well-tested or official, but here's an example of doing that in one application: https://github.com/trestletech/shiny-sandbox/blob/master/grn/ui.R#L7. You would obviously want to change the GA ID you're using there.

My suspicion is that the rga package may be used to doing analysis on the traffic you've already collected in GA. So perhaps you'll find it useful after setting up the GA JavaScript on an app using one of the above techniques.

Best,
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Reload an animated gif
messages.body_plain:
To answer my own post above, it looks like there are some caching features that I didn't fully understand.  In particular:

1. It seems that, if an animated gif has already been displayed in a shiny app, the animation cannot be repeated (assuming the gif does not loop).

2. If you create a copy of the original animated gif (same file, different filename), shiny seems to recognize that the copy is identical to the original.  When the animation displays for one of these files in a shiny app, the animation from both files cease to display thereafter (this is the caching part that I don't fully understand).

3. To get the same animation to display twice, I had to create two animated gifs, with one having a slightly smaller dimension than the other.  Now, the file sizes differ and they are not recognized as identical.

messages.subject: Re: Custom fonts with shiny server?
messages.body_plain:
Here is a minimal example

require(shiny)
runApp(list(
  ui = bootstrapPage(
    tags$link(
      rel = "stylesheet",
      href="http://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Open+Sans"
    ),
    tags$style("h1{font-family: 'Open Sans'}"),
    tags$h1("Test Font"),
    numericInput('n', 'Number of obs', 100),
    plotOutput('plot')
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$plot <- renderPlot({ hist(runif(input$n)) })
  }
))

messages.subject: Re: Best Practices: Reactivity
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andres, thanks for the thoughtful and detailed questions.

> I find that in order to eliminate errors I have to throw {return(invisible())} all over the place.

Rather than testing on input$x and input$y for null, I tend to have each chunk of code only test for null on its direct dependencies--in this case, reactiveThing. (Note that it's relatively cheap to call reactiveThing() twice since it automatically caches its results.)

That being said, I don't think this situation is ideal, since the whole chain of dependencies needs to have this "Is it null? then return NULL" logic. I've been thinking for a while that we should have a special condition/error that indicates that a calculation is missing its prerequisites, so that reactiveThing() could be something like

reactiveThing <- reactive({
  if (is.null(input$x) || is.null(input$y)) {
    signalCancel()
  }
  # Do stuff...
})

where signalCancel would essentially throw a unique error that doesn't show up in the UI as a red error message. That way, anything that directly or indirectly depends on reactiveThing would automatically inherit this behavior, unless they explicitly wrap that part of the code with tryCatch or whatever.

Would welcome any thoughts about this.

As for the second part of your e-mail, if you mean that when you switch between tabs you sometimes see old/stale results before they update, that is probably because by default outputs are lazy-loading; if they are not visible, they don't recalculate. You can change this behavior on an output-by-output basis by using outputOptions, specifically the suspendWhenHidden option.

On Thu, Oct 17, 2013 at 9:07 AM, Andres Fonseca <clubaf...@gmail.com> wrote:

> How do you guys structure efficient code? I find that I write a lot of stuff that ends up working but I'm unconvinced it is the most efficient way of doing things.
> For instance, I have a lot of code in server.r that looks like
>
> output$title1 <- renderText({
> if (is.null(input$x)| is.null(input$y)) {return(invisible())}
> temp <- myfunction(reactiveThing())       #reactiveThing depends of input$x and input$y
> sprintf('myNumber is %s', temp)
> })
>
> I find that in order to eliminate errors I have to throw {return(invisible())} all over the place. Is that a good idea or am I missing a better way of managing dependencies?
> Also, and I'm not sure if this is related, I find that if a tab has a couple reactive elements, that they respond to changes at different times and will often display my error messages like
>
> output$Error <- renderText({
> if (is.null(input$x) | is.null(input$y)) {return(invisible())}
> if(nrow(reactiveTable()) < 1) {return('No Data within Date Range for this View')} #reactiveTable is dependent on x and y
> })
>
> for a moment and then get reset.
>

messages.subject: Re: Best Practices: Reactivity
messages.body_plain:
Joe:

I assume you mean that you put the is.null(input$x) inside reactiveThing(). myfunction then has to check if the return from reactiveThing is a null.

Caching of reactives is great but if reactiveThing returns a big datasets calling it is not that cheap ... or is it?

Not having the red-errors pop-up would be great :)

On Thursday, October 17, 2013 10:47:46 AM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Hi Andres, thanks for the thoughtful and detailed questions.
>
> > I find that in order to eliminate errors I have to throw {return(invisible())} all over the place.
>
> Rather than testing on input$x and input$y for null, I tend to have each chunk of code only test for null on its direct dependencies--in this case, reactiveThing. (Note that it's relatively cheap to call reactiveThing() twice since it automatically caches its results.)
>
> That being said, I don't think this situation is ideal, since the whole chain of dependencies needs to have this "Is it null? then return NULL" logic. I've been thinking for a while that we should have a special condition/error that indicates that a calculation is missing its prerequisites, so that reactiveThing() could be something like
>
> reactiveThing <- reactive({
>   if (is.null(input$x) || is.null(input$y)) {
>     signalCancel()
>   }
>   # Do stuff...
> })
>
> where signalCancel would essentially throw a unique error that doesn't show up in the UI as a red error message. That way, anything that directly or indirectly depends on reactiveThing would automatically inherit this behavior, unless they explicitly wrap that part of the code with tryCatch or whatever.
>
> Would welcome any thoughts about this.
>
> As for the second part of your e-mail, if you mean that when you switch between tabs you sometimes see old/stale results before they update, that is probably because by default outputs are lazy-loading; if they are not visible, they don't recalculate. You can change this behavior on an output-by-output basis by using outputOptions, specifically the suspendWhenHidden option.
>
>
> On Thu, Oct 17, 2013 at 9:07 AM, Andres Fonseca <clubaf...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > temp <- myfunction(reactiveThing())       #reactiveThing depends of input$x and input$y
> > sprintf('myNumber is %s', temp)
> > })
> >

> > })
> >
> > for a moment and then get reset.

messages.subject: Re: upload data
messages.body_plain:
The data is copied as a temp file. If you want to keep it, you have to copy it somewhere more permanent. In your server.R you could do something like:

observe({
  if (!is.null(input$file1)) {
    file.copy(input$file1$datapath, tempfile(tmpdir="~/uploads/", fileext=".csv"))
  }
})

messages.subject: Input object appears not to be available until called a second time
messages.subject_clean: Input object appears not to be available until called a second time
messages.body_plain:
I created a StackOverflow post about creating a dynamic number of inputSlider object when the number required is not known in advance:
- http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19130455/create-dynamic-number-of-input-elements-with-r-shiny

I got great advice and attempted to implement it. The full post is there, but the summary is that I'm doing the following:

ui.R
----------
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Side by side comparison"),

  sidebarPanel(

    sliderInput(inputId = "members", label = "Number of individuals on plan:",
                min = 1, max = 15, value = 2, step = 1),

    sliderInput(inputId = "max_pred", label = "Maximum for expense range:",
                min = 5000, max = 100000, value = 5000, step = 5000),

    uiOutput("sliders")

    ),

  mainPanel(
      plotOutput(outputId = "main_plot", width = "100%"))
)))

server.R
----------
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$sliders <- renderUI({
    members <- as.integer(input$members)
    max_pred <- as.integer(input$max_pred)
    lapply(1:members, function(i) {
      sliderInput(inputId = paste0("ind", i), label = paste("Individual", i),
                  min = 0, max = max_pred, value = c(0, 500), step = 100)
    })

  })

  expenses <- reactive({
    print(names(input))
    members <- as.numeric(input$members)

    mins <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[1]
    })

    maxs <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[2]
    })

    expenses <- as.data.frame(cbind(mins, maxs))
  })

  best_case <- reactive({

    expenses <- expenses()
    ...
    ...
  })

That's enough to explain the problem. I got errors about applying a non-function and started digging around a bit. I used browser() inside the expenses <- reactive({}) bit above and was perplexed by the fact that ls() didn't show an input or output object existing. I tried putting print(names(input)) at the top of it, and got *two* print-outs in the session window:
[1] "class"    "max_pred" "members"
[1] "class"    "ind1"     "ind2"     "max_pred" "members"

I did the same for print(expenses) and also got two:
# the first
  mins maxs
1   NA   NA
2   NA   NA

# the second
  mins maxs
1    0  500
2    0  500

So, it's making me think something's goofy about my expenses definition, or that somehow the outputUI bit hasn't done it's thing by the time expenses is run, but *does* get run when I run the line `expenses <- expenses()` and re-call it.

Any suggestions? I have no idea how to troubleshoot this one!

Thanks,
John

To help you debug and understand your dependencies, simply put options(shiny.reactlog=TRUE); after library(shiny) in your server.R code and press Ctrl+F3 in your browser and see.

Also the code re-uses the name expenses in a few instances. Not sure if it's a problem but to avoid confusion may I suggest you use different names. E.g. you have expenses <- expenses(), why not just expenses_result <- expenses().

I believe ls() show you only the objects that exists in the current environment, so ls() won't show you input output.

I suspect there is nothing goofy about the double print. When shiny starts everything is run once to help it determine the dependencies. The first time it runs input$members is null so it prints the first time. Then I suppose some where in your code input$members is updated which causes expenses to run a second time. Try this to see if it explains.

expenses <- reactive({
    print(names(input))
    members <- as.numeric(input$members)

    mins <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[1]
    })

    maxs <- sapply(1:members, function(i) {
      as.numeric(input[[paste0("ind", i)]])[2]
    })

    expenses_result <- as.data.frame(cbind(mins, maxs))
    print("Finished running once")
    expenses_result

  })

messages.subject: Re: Getting ImpactStory JavaScript widgets rendered to a table cell
messages.subject_clean: Getting ImpactStory JavaScript widgets rendered to a table cell
messages.body_plain:
Well, I've found one solution that isn't pretty but will do for the moment.

renderTable uses xtable to render the HTML table, and you can define your own sanitization function while at it, see http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/xtable/vignettes/xtableGallery.pdf (p. 7)

Here, I simply replace the column header 'Widget' with a string that defines the script:

output$table <- renderTable({
   ...
  }, include.rownames = FALSE, sanitize.text.function = function(s) sub("Widget", "<script type=\"text/javascript\" src=\"http://impactstory.org/embed/v1/impactstory.js\ <http://impactstory.org/embed/v1/impactstory.js%5C>"></script>", s))

For a reason I don't yet understand, there is a set of double widgets at first.

Thanks for your patience.

How does one actually access the reactive elements created (I suppose the point in reactiveUI isn't *just* to make the form change, but to actually access the dynamically created results!)??

John

messages.subject: Re: Dynamic input and output
messages.body_plain:
>From R Help

? local

local evaluates an expression in a local environment. It is equivalent to evalq except that its default argument creates a new, empty environment. This is useful to create anonymous recursive functions and as a kind of limited namespace feature since variables defined in the environment are not visible from the outside.

messages.subject: css to set table class to table-condensed (bootstrap)
messages.subject_clean: css to set table class to table-condensed (bootstrap)
messages.body_plain:
Perhaps a bit off-topic but ...

I am using pander for conditional formatting of tables in a Shiny app. Pander creates the relevant markdown and then I use markdownToHTML to create the html the app will display (see command below).

html <- markdownToHTML(text = fancyTab, stylesheet="www/fancyTab.css")

mardownToHTML allows you to specify a css file to apply when creating the html. I like boostrap's 'table-condensed' class and would like to apply that. I assume there is a simple way to put that in a css file but I haven't been able to find it. I resorted to the following hack. Any better alternatives?

html <- gsub("<table>","<table class='table table-condensed'>", html)

Screenshot attached.

messages.subject_clean: Is there a way when you close google chrome, your R is automatically closed?
messages.body_plain:
Alternatively, you could add a "stopApp()" call on a particular button. It's an extra step, but the code would be dead easy.

Finally, are you aware of Shiny Server <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/>? It will handle the startup and shutdown of R processes as needed -- so an R process would be spawned when you visited your app's URL, then be terminated once you closed the window (with no additional coding on your part). It looks like you're on Windows, which we don't yet support, so you'd likely need a virtual machine to get this running on your desktop. May be more trouble than it's worth for a single app, but if you find that you regularly are starting up and shutting down apps, it's something to keep in mind.

Jeff

messages.subject: New features for Shiny 0.8.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

We're hoping to submit Shiny 0.8.0 to CRAN very shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we've added since 0.7.0. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub:

    if (!require(devtools))
      install.packages('devtools')
    install.packages('httpuv')
    devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

RStudio users should also install the latest v0.98.443 Preview Release, which is available here: http://www.rstudio.com/ide/download/preview

New debugging features

In this release of Shiny we've greatly improved the set of debugging tools you can use with your Shiny apps. It's now much easier to figure out what's happening when things go wrong, thanks to two new features:
Integration with the new visual debugger that's available with RStudio v0.98. You can set breakpoints and step through your code much more easily than before.
A new option 'shiny.error' which can take a function as an error handler. It is called when an error occurs in a reactive observer (e.g. when running an output rendering function). You can use options(shiny.error=traceback) to simply print a traceback, options(shiny.error=recover) for debugging from a regular R console, or options(shiny.error=browser) to jump into the RStudio visual debugger.
We're especially interested in feedback for these debugging features -- please do try them and let us know whether you find them useful!

DataTables integration

Shiny 0.8.0 will support much more attractive and powerful displays of tabular data using the popular DataTables <http://datatables.net/> library. Our DataTables integration features pagination, searching/filtering, sorting, and more. Check out this demo <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/yihui/12_datatables/> to see it in action, and learn more about how to use it in your own apps by visiting the tutorial's chapter on DataTables <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#datatables> (you may need to refresh your web browser if you cannot see this chapter).

There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at our NEWS file <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/NEWS> (you see v0.7.0.99 there but it will turn to v0.8.0 on CRAN).

Thanks for your support -- we look forward to hearing from you!

-- The Shiny team

If the former then consider using a memoized <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/memoise/index.html> function that is declared at the location that you pointed out in your email ("I know this would work:").

If the latter, then perhaps make each of your queries its own reactive, and have the "data" reactive use each of them when appropriate.

Hope that helps...?

messages.subject: Is there a recommended pattern for checking whether a user has ever interacted with a widget?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a recommended pattern for checking whether a user has ever interacted with a widget?
messages.body_plain:
Motivation: For widgets that start initialized to a particular value, it can be unclear whether they are that way because the user happened to choose that same value or because the user has not yet interacted with them. An example of a widget where this is an issue is sliderInput().

I tried having the initial values of sliderInput be ones that are forbidden by the step argument, so the user could put the slider close to where it had been but not on that exact spot. For example... sliderInput('foo','My slider:',min=-1,max=1,value=c(-.999,.999),step=0.1) ...but it appears that the starting values get rounded to legal ones and I still cannot detect a difference.

Do I need to delve into custom Javascript to detect clicks on that widget or an extra widget that specifically asks the user if they intended to ignore the slider values? Or is there some kind of more elegant pattern for distinguishing "virgin" sliders from ones set back to initial values?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Is there a recommended pattern for checking whether a user has ever interacted with a widget?
messages.subject_clean: Is there a recommended pattern for checking whether a user has ever interacted with a widget?
messages.body_plain:
I'm plotting various residuals and trying to get the user to give their subjective assessment of where in the support range the residuals of a statistical model begin to diverge from what would be expected if the model's assumptions are correct. The sliders give them feedback by updating the plots with lines superimposed indicating the area the user has selected, and report to the app the user's beliefs about the residuals.

So, this guides them through the process the statisticians I know use in practice: eyeballing. But if they didn't play with the residuals at all, the app should interpret that as no answer rather than the initial values happening to be the range.

Another widget where this can happen is the checkbox-- did the user mean  "no" or "no comment".

Now, I can probably think of a different workaround of varying confusingness for each widget. For example sliders can be initialized to some almost-always obviously wrong value, and checkboxes can be replaced with select menus that have "pick one" as the default and the observers always check for it. So this might not be as crucial a feature as it seemed before I thought about it some more. But if you know of some sort of internal counter or flag that already does this and its just a matter of exposing it or documenting it, it would be nice to have and would allow cleaner code inside server.R

messages.subject: Re: Problem with updateSelectInput
messages.body_plain:
I have just run into this bug as well. The problem with the suggested workaround is that it relies on having the values for choices accessible to server.R. This introduces unnecessary overhead and redundancy if you don't need to alter the choices, all you need to do is change which choice is selected. This is especially a problem if your selectInput() widgets are static HTML or (were) contained entirely in ui.R. I notice that at the end of the updateSelectInput() function, there is the following line: session$sendInputMessage(inputId,message); inputId is the same as the argument to updateSelectInput() and message is an object with the following structure: List of 1 $ options:List of 2 ..$ :List of 3 .. ..$ value : chr "x" .. ..$ label : chr "x" .. ..$ selected: logi FALSE ..$ :List of 3 .. ..$ value : chr "y" .. ..$ label : chr "y" .. ..$ selected: logi FALSE ...where options is an un-named list that can contain an arbitrary number of these triplets. Experimenting has revealed that if I manually use session$sendInputMessage with a message whose options only include the selections I want to update, the target list gets updated such that those become the only choices. Does this mean that bug #176 actually runs deeper than updateSelectInput and is caused by whatever is listening to sendInputMessage having to rewrite the entire selectInput if any part of it is updated? messages.body_plain:
Even if there was a counter or a flag, wouldn't it be possible that users would see that the slider range is set to the range that they already thought was appropriate, and leave it untouched?

What if instead of a slider, they had to click twice on the plot to specify the range? No clicks would then be an unambigious indicator.

On Thu, Oct 24, 2013 at 4:22 AM, Alex Bokov <alex....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I'm plotting various residuals and trying to get the user to give their subjective assessment of where in the support range the residuals of a statistical model begin to diverge from what would be expected if the model's assumptions are correct. The sliders give them feedback by updating the plots with lines superimposed indicating the area the user has selected, and report to the app the user's beliefs about the residuals.
>
> So, this guides them through the process the statisticians I know use in practice: eyeballing. But if they didn't play with the residuals at all, the app should interpret that as no answer rather than the initial values happening to be the range.
>
> Another widget where this can happen is the checkbox-- did the user mean  "no" or "no comment".
>
> Now, I can probably think of a different workaround of varying confusingness for each widget. For example sliders can be initialized to some almost-always obviously wrong value, and checkboxes can be replaced with select menus that have "pick one" as the default and the observers always check for it. So this might not be as crucial a feature as it seemed before I thought about it some more. But if you know of some sort of internal counter or flag that already does this and its just a matter of exposing it or documenting it, it would be nice to have and would allow cleaner code inside server.R

library(shiny)

messages.subject: Re: trouble with conditional sidebar panel
messages.body_plain:
I'll defer to the experts but I believe you need a tabsetPanel id statement immediately below mainPanel instead of the initial tabsetPanel you currently have there.

Here's an example:

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel('Test Reports'),
  sidebarPanel(
    conditionalPanel(
condition = "input.tabs1 == 1",
checkboxGroupInput('show_vars1', 'Select Columns to Display:', names(FirstTable),
selected = names(FirstTable)),
helpText('Data updated daily.')
    ),
    conditionalPanel(
condition = "input.tabs1 == 2",
checkboxGroupInput('show_vars2', 'Select Columns to Display:', names(SecondTable),
selected = names(SecondTable)),
helpText('Data updated daily.')
    )
  ),

  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(id ="tabs1",
        tabPanel('FirstTable', dataTableOutput("mytable1"), value = 1),
        tabPanel('SecondTable', dataTableOutput("mytable2"), value = 2)
    )
  )
))

messages.body_plain:
Hi Alexey,

That is a central problem with R's single-threaded model. There have been a few workarounds proposed on the mailing list previously.

The formal solution to this problem will be Shiny Server Professional, which supports a configurable number of processes per Shiny applications (one process per app, one process per visitor, or anything in between). If you're interested in getting more details, please contact Tareef Kawaf (tar...@rstudio.com) who would be happy to get you some more info on the product.

Best,
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: sh: R: command not found
messages.body_plain:
So it turns out that this is a simple path export issue.

The environment that the init.d/shiny-server script was being call in could no see /usr/local/bin

Adding the following line to the top of the script fixed the matter:
PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/bin"

Hi Joe,

I am running into then same issue. The standard browser is IE 9, I do not have AdMin rights to change this. But obviously there are portable browser versions (e.g. Chrome) available, which can be used without installation.
Is it possible to tell Shiny (perhaps in the future) which browser Shiny should use to override the standard web browser? My attempts with options(browser... and Sys.setenviron("R_BROWSER" = .... were not successful.

Thank you very much for your advice.

Jürgen

Am Dienstag, 9. Juli 2013 14:13:02 UTC+2 schrieb Joe Cheng [RStudio]:
> Thanks for the feedback, noted.
>
> In case it wasn't clear, Shiny apps do support IE8 & 9 when deployed using Shiny Server. It's only when developing or using Shiny apps locally without going through Shiny Server that those browsers don't work.
>
> On Tuesday, July 9, 2013 1:03:13 PM UTC+2, Joachim Johansson wrote:
> > Hi Joe,
> >
> > Shiny can certainly add a lot of value for many companies. However, in my experience, IT departments for large corporations will be quite inflexible regarding which browsers (and plug-ins) they support. It also goes without saying that many IT departments will favour Microsoft solutions, basically because their staff will usually have invested heavily into learning about Microsoft products.
> >
> > For those reasons, I think Shiny would be more widely adopted if it would support IE9 and newer browsers.
> >
> > Kind regards,
> > Joachim - Zürich
> >
> > On Friday, November 9, 2012 1:33:07 AM UTC+1, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > Sorry, I think we forgot to document this--we have serious compatibility issues with IE9 and below. That's a pretty big oversight, we'll try to correct that soon.
> > > IE8 currently doesn't work with either Shiny running locally, or Shiny server (e.g. our live example apps on the Shiny homepages).
> > > IE9 currently doesn't work with Shiny running locally, but it does work with Shiny server.
> > > IE10 should work fine with both versions of Shiny.
> > > If you can install Chrome Frame <http://www.google.com/chromeframe> for IE (any supported version), then both versions of Shiny will work.
> > > Please let us know if this is a problem for you, including what version of IE you need support for, and whether it's an option for your users to install a more up-to-date browser. If IE compatibility is really going to stop adoption of Shiny in companies then we would consider tackling the quite significant engineering tasks needed to solve these compatibility issues. But of course that means time we couldn't spend improving the rest of the framework. So we definitely need your feedback to help us prioritize.
> > >
> > > (In case you are interested in the technical details, Shiny relies heavily on a feature of HTML5 called Websockets. IE8 and 9 don't support websockets; Microsoft used to have a free plugin for IE9 that enabled websocket support, but they seem to have pulled it down since IE10 was released. Shiny server works around this limitation by using communication platforms from other languages (that isn't available in R) that it translates to/from websocket traffic. That's why IE9 works on Shiny server but not locally. IE8 doesn't even work on Shiny server because of a different, unrelated issue <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3586749/how-to-get-around-ie8-32k-limit-on-datauri-on-base64-encode>.)
> > >
> > > Thanks for the question!

messages.subject: Re: tutorial examples not working with internet explorer 9 as default browser.
messages.subject_clean: tutorial examples not working with internet explorer 9 as default browser.
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I think, I have found a workaround for me.

As a reminder:
Shiny (used locally) would like to use the standard web browser. In our cooperate environment we are working with IE 9 as standard browser without having the possibility to change to another browser. And... IE 9 is not suitable for Shiny used without Shiny Server.
But, it is possible to work with e.g. Chrome as portable web browser.

Using Shiny will start IE 9, the app will not work properly and error messages will pop up in the console of R. If one opens additionally http://localhost:8100 in Chrome, the app is working fine (at least for me) in Chrome.

Perhaps this approach is helpful for others as well.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject_clean: Is there a way when you close google chrome, your R is automatically closed?
messages.body_plain:
No, and I don't think there's even a way in a webpage, period, to distinguish between the two. You could use a heuristic on the server side like "If another session isn't started within 1 second then it's closed", I suppose. I strongly suspect that's possible to implement using Shiny's reactive primitives but I don't have an implementation of that off the top of my head.

messages.subject: Re: R shiny with connection pool
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bruno,

I don't know whether or not connection pooling is easily available for MySQL in R, but Shiny wouldn't limit you in this. You would just want to make sure that your connection pool were properly scoped (http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping). i.e. you weren't setting up a new connection pool for every Shiny session, but rather had a global pool that was shared between all sessions.

Hopefully someone else can steer you in the right direction regarding MySQL connection pooling in R!

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Hi Stephane,

Thanks for the feedback, these are great finds!

Some workarounds for now, if these are hampering your productivity:

1) If your breakpoints seem out of sync with the document, restarting the R session should fix the problem (use Session -> Restart R)

2) If there are so many environments in the drop list that you can't pick the one you want, you can remove items you don't need from the list. What's displayed there is effectively the output of search() plus debug context environments, so you can trim it down by using detach() to remove package environments.

I've filed a couple of internal bugs based on the problems you've found, and we hope to have them fixed soon.

Thanks,
Jonathan.

I am consistently getting this error right after runApp() with window graying out.

have to do with leftover reactive expressions and observers. We've
been considering ways to fix the issue, but haven't settled on a good
solution yet.

One workaround which usually works is to run the following a few times
after your app stops. It should clear out old reactive expressions and
observers:
  shiny:::flushReact()

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: What AWS instance tpe for shiny-server ?
messages.subject_clean: What AWS instance tpe for shiny-server ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yann,

I'm not sure about the exact instance types for Spark/Glimmer, but I've been running a Shiny Server on an "m1.small x64" AWS instance with pretty good performance. (http://trestletechnology.net:3838/reactiveGeyeser/) After app startup time, the responsiveness seems to be pretty good (at least from the US, where the server is).

We are gradually working towards some features that would offer insight into the performance of Shiny apps, but we don't really have anything useful ready just yet.

A couple of additional thoughts:
I've heard that AWS instances can vary drastically in terms of their performance. Sometimes you'll get put on a box which is oversubscribed for CPU and/or bandwidth and your instance won't perform very well. The suggestion I've heard in such instances is to shut down the machine and bring up another one to try again.
You could try loading some static assets form your apps to test the performance independent of any Shiny reactivity. For instance, I can open http://trestletechnology.net:3838/reactiveGeyeser/shared/bootstrap/css/bootstrap-responsive.min.css on my server with the network tab open in Google Chrome to see exactly how long it's taking to load a simple, static file. If it's taking a long time to open a small, static file on an otherwise idle server, that may indicate that your EC2 instance doesn't have the appropriate CPU or Bandwidth to be able to perform well. If that file does load quickly, that may indict the Shiny application's performance. If that were the case, it may be worthwhile to profile your Shiny app more closely to see where the slowdown might be.
Best,
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: spark RStudio error: unsupported URL scheme
messages.subject_clean: spark RStudio error: unsupported URL scheme
messages.body_plain:
To add on to what Jeff said: https downloads are tricky in R (with R's
built-in download.file function), and they are handled by separate
code paths on Mac, Windows, and Linux, so that may explain why it's
different from your desktop RStudio. For example, an https download of
the Google homepage fails on Spark:
  > download.file('https://google.com/', 'test.html')
  Error in download.file("https://google.com/", "test.html") :
    unsupported URL scheme

The downloader package tries to work around these differences on the
different platforms, to make it possible to consistently to use https.
To use it:

install.packages('downloader')
library(downloader)
download('https://google.com/', 'test.html')

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
I think the lack of alpha support has something to do with the devices supported on your system. If I remember correctly, if your server was compiled with cairo support, it will have transparency support, and it should default to using that when it generates PNG files. If it doesn't have cairo support, then it will use xlib, which doesn't support transparency.

One workaround is to install the Cairo package on your system or user account. (Note that this is different from having R compiled with cairo support -- the Cairo package provides the Cairo::CairoPNG() function which can be used instead of png() when creating png files.) When the Cairo package is installed, Shiny will detect it and use
CairoPNG, which has transparency support.

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
At the moment, the search text is treated as regular expressions in R
by default, and there are a couple of features that are not
implemented yet on shiny's side. For your case, a probably awkward
solution is to use regular expressions like [Aa]pple to search for
"apple" or "Apple". Unfortunately, the DataTables library does not
seem to pass the bCaseInsensitive option to the server side
(http://datatables.net/usage/server-side), so we cannot make use of it
(note that renderDataTable() uses server-side processing, i.e. it is R
that processes the data).

messages.subject: Re: reactivity question
messages.body_plain:
It is hard to read the reactlog because there are many nodes in the graph. But I have not seen the node corresponding to ratioTable().

I have tried the following experiment. I put a debugging point at the last line of ratioTable():

> ratioTable <- reactive[{
>    ...
>    outputobject # DEBUGGING POINT HERE
> })

Then I try the app using either observer 1 or observer 2 :

  observe({  # observer 1

    if(is.null(getBreaks())) return(NULL)
    bounds <- isolate(ratioTable())
    updateTextInput(session, "sub", value=attr(bounds,"run"))
  })

  observe({  # observer 2

    if(is.null(getBreaks())) return(NULL)
    bounds <- ratioTable()
    updateTextInput(session, "sub", value=attr(bounds,"run"))
  })

With observer 1, no debugging occurs when I modify the sub input, whereas the debugging occurs with observer 2.
